mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active and the direction of the proxy (FEDFUNDS) is negative: lower rates predict positive returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in < 60% of instances or the Rank IC over 3 years is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index level above 230.0 signals persistent inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The trigger condition is CPIAUCSL > 230.0.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in < 40% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 230.0) or the Rank IC over 3 years is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5.0% and housing starts (HOUST) exceed 650.0 thousand units, it signals a strong labor market and robust housing demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active only when both conditions are met.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in < 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE < 5.0 AND HOUST > 650.0) or the Rank IC over 3 years is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS rising > 0.5% over 3 months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in < 40% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% in 3 months) or the Rank IC over 3 years is < 0.03.
